context:
Goal: no lane waits on a conflicting neighbour in the batch.
Problem (rule): batch runner 10's pairwise check found lanes that touch the same files: merge/merge.py (#3231, #3175, #3235, #3049, #3230), hooks/guard.py (#3223, #2691), checks.yml (#3216, #3250), shoot (#3214 against #2716 and #2717). Your standing grant lets the runner merge main into a handed-in branch only. Merging one lane's head into another lane's branch is a different act, so it needs your word.
Based on (read): runner 10's message 14:13 CST, relayed by the coordinator 14:22 CST; decision standing-merge-grant. Your words 14:13 CST, relayed: "batch overlaps pre-addressed so no lane waits". Option a makes the second PR of a pair wait one batch, so it fits those words only in part.
Based on (ruling): step post-batch-conflict-merge (done): after a batch merges, each lane PR that now conflicts gets one main merge and a hunks-only review. No past ruling found that covers a lane-to-lane merge.
Departs from: main — the runner merges only main into a branch; option b also lets it merge a neighbour lane's head.
Meanwhile: the coordinator keeps going; no pair rides one batch until you answer.

options.gain: No PR depends on another unmerged PR.
options.label: No widening: a conflicting pair goes to different batches, in order (Recommended)
options.lose: The second PR of each pair waits one batch.

options.label: Builders merge one lane's head into the other's branch, under the grant's limits
options.lose: The two PRs become dependent: neither merges without the other. Limits: no push within 2 h, no rebase or force, a behaviour-changing conflict goes to the coordinator, a fix check and fresh record after. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

reply: Withdrawn as moot, 14:25 CST: runner 10 withdrew its ask at 14:14 CST after 105 merge-tree checks over 14 hand-ins found no conflicts. Still unchecked: #3214 against #2716 and #2717, and the 14 against batch 139's lanes. No answer needed.
short: Batch overlaps: separate batches, or merge lane heads?
title: How should the batch runner handle lanes that overlap: separate batches, or merge one lane's head into another's?
why: Option b widens the standing merge grant from main-into-branch to lane-into-lane, which needs your word.
